title: Rebecca at the well (Genesis 24)
hook: a servant prays for a sign and a young woman waters ten camels

segments.voice: Yesterday, God will provide: a father and son walking up a hill, and a ram in a thicket. Did the line help with a need you couldn't meet yet? Today Isaac is grown, and someone goes looking for his wife. Day three hundred fifty-three.

Genesis twenty-four is a long chapter, and its hero doesn't even get a name. He's the elder servant of Abraham's house, the one in charge of everything. Abraham, very old now, sends him back to the old country in Mesopotamia to find a wife for Isaac among his own relatives. The servant loads ten camels with gifts and makes the long trip. He arrives at evening, at a well outside the city, at the hour the women come out to draw water. And he has no idea what he's looking for. So he does the only thing he can think of. He prays.
screen: `A SERVANT WITH NO NAME.` → `SENT BACK TO THE OLD COUNTRY.` → `TEN CAMELS AT A WELL.`

segments.voice: First, the prayer. He asks God to show kindness to his master, and he names a sign. Let the young woman to whom I say, let down thy pitcher that I may drink, be the one who answers: drink, and I'll give thy camels drink also. Notice what he's asking for. Not beauty, not wealth. A generous heart. Second, the answer. Before he's even finished praying, Rebecca comes out with a pitcher on her shoulder. He runs to her and asks for a little water. She lowers the jar and gives it to him. And then, in the Douay-Rheims: "And when he had drunk, she said: I will draw water for thy camels also, till they all drink." Third, the size of that offer. Ten camels after a desert journey. She runs back and forth to the well, emptying her jar into the trough, again and again, until every one is done. Nobody asked her to. That's the sign: not that she gave water, but that she did more than she was asked. The servant stands there and watches in silence, wondering. Fourth, the choice. When the family discusses it, they end by asking her. Will you go with this man? And Rebecca says, in the Douay-Rheims: "I will go." Just that. Another person leaving home for a land she hasn't seen, like Abraham before her. The servant bows to the ground and thanks God, whose kindness, he says, has led him the whole way.
screen: `HE PRAYS FOR A GENEROUS HEART.` · `SHE COMES BEFORE HE FINISHES.` · `TEN THIRSTY CAMELS.` · `THEY ASK HER: WILL YOU GO?` · then, large: `THY CAMELS ALSO.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: do more than you're asked. Settle, and breathe. Think of one request you know is coming in the next day. A coworker needs a file. A kid needs help with homework. Your partner asks you to pick up milk. Now picture Rebecca at the trough, jar after jar. What's the camels-too version of that request? Sending the file and offering to look it over. Picking up the milk and the thing they forgot. Choose one. If you pray, you can ask for a generous heart like hers. The bell holds the time.
Rebecca at the well. The young woman who gave a stranger water and then watered all ten of his camels, and later said, I will go.
Your line: the camels too. Today, when someone asks you for one thing, give it, and then quietly do the next thing they'll need. Day three hundred fifty-three.

howItsDone: Catholics remember Rebecca among the matriarchs of faith, and Genesis 24 is one of the Old Testament readings the Church offers for weddings.

myth: the servant asks God for a beautiful wife for Isaac
he asks for a sign of a generous heart: the one who offers water to his camels too.
Rebecca's family asks her whether she will go
the servant in Genesis 24 is named in the chapter
he's only called Abraham's servant. later tradition often calls him Eliezer.

fork.setup: you're at the well with your water jar. a tired stranger with ten camels asks for a little water. what do you do?
options: give him a drink and go home.
give him a drink, then water all ten camels.
point him to the trough and let him do it himself.
fork.reveal: "I will draw water for thy camels also, till they all drink." she did more than she was asked, and that was the sign.

original.note: Hebrew: kindness, faithful love. the servant asks God to show it to his master, and thanks God for it at the end.

trapdoor: what you thought: a story about an arranged marriage.
what it means: a servant prays for a generous heart, and a young woman shows it by doing far more than she's asked, then chooses to go.
what a scholar hears: chesed, faithful kindness, runs through the chapter from the servant's prayer to his thanks.

sources.quoted: And when he had drunk, she said: I will draw water for thy camels also, till they all drink.

notes: Douay-Rheims Genesis 24:19 and 24:58 quoted from memory; confirm wording.
Genesis 24 as the longest chapter in Genesis (67 verses): confirm.
The servant is unnamed in chapter 24; tradition links him with Eliezer of 15:2. Confirm.
'A thirsty camel can drink many gallons': deliberately unquantified. Confirm.
howItsDone: Genesis 24:48–51, 58–67 is an option in the Catholic wedding lectionary; confirm.
